clue.text: Fortune left to a section of the church

parts.note: fortune in the sense of luck is chance

explanation.surface: A windfall bequeathed to part of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: A shocking accusation?

parts.note: an electrical sense of something that gives a shock, combined with a formal allegation of a crime

explanation.definitionFit: A charge is both an electrical quantity that can give a shock and a formal allegation of wrongdoing.

clue.text: The play has now begun, and should be heard by a judge

definitions.text: should be heard by a judge

explanation.surface: A drama's opening night, with a court case looming.
explanation.walkthrough: A film director calls the word to start a scene; a legal suit is heard in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The director's call to start filming, and a lawsuit brought before a court.

clue.text: His chilling tales could make anyone cold

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be rebuilt into a new name

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A writer's spooky stories could send a shiver through any reader.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Conan Doyle wrote Sherlock Holmes stories and also tales of terror and the supernatural.
explanation.definitionFit: The creator of Sherlock Holmes also wrote many stories of horror and the uncanny.

clue.text: A flower which means much to you and me

parts.note: a lot means much
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A bloom that holds great meaning for the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, sacred in Asian religions.

clue.text: Raises one's eyes heavenward and recovers

explanation.surface: Someone glances skyward in relief as things improve.
explanation.definitionFit: To look up is literally to raise the gaze, and figuratively to improve, as trade or health does when it picks up.

clue.text: Take to a photograph in a flash

parts.note: to take to someone is to like them
a photograph is a shot

explanation.surface: Falling for a picture the moment the flashbulb goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a shot is an idiom for instantly, without hesitation.

clue.text: Drive out from Houston

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the letters of the city name

explanation.surface: Expelling someone from the Texas city.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to expel or force someone from a position.

clue.text: Appeared embarrassed

explanation.surface: Someone turned up and was humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: Showed up means arrived or appeared, and also exposed or shamed someone.

clue.text: Possible to accommodate cattle in cramped conditions

indicators.note: one word takes in another, holding it inside

parts.note: poss is a short form of possible
kine is an old plural of cow, meaning cattle

explanation.surface: Trying to fit livestock into a tight space.
explanation.definitionFit: Pokiness is the quality of being small and cramped, as a poky room is.

clue.text: I leave two in a London borough

indicators.note: the letter I is told to leave, so it is removed from the referenced word

parts.note: a cross-reference to the answer of 2-down, which is the word action
taken as written

explanation.surface: A resident departs from a pair of homes in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' points to 2-down (ACTION); when its I leaves, ACTON remains. Acton is a district of west London, in the borough of Ealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a district of west London, treated by the setter as a borough of the capital.

clue.text: Become a shoplifter, but weigh up the pros and cons

definitions.text: weigh up the pros and cons

explanation.surface: A thief deliberates before pocketing goods from a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, a shoplifter steals the shop's merchandise; idiomatically, to pause and assess a situation carefully.

clue.text: Pitch supervisor stops a pilot flying

explanation.surface: A sports-field keeper prevents an aviator from taking off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: to stop a pilot flying is to ground the man, read as 'grounds man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundsman maintains a sports pitch; and one who grounds an airman keeps him out of the sky.

clue.text: Piercing lament

explanation.surface: A sharp, shrill wail of grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen means sharp or penetrating, and as a noun an Irish wailing dirge for the dead.

clue.text: Likely to get roasted or boiled?

definitions.text: Likely to get roasted or boiled?

parts.words: Likely to get roasted or boiled?
parts.note: read as cooking, but to be roasted is also to be severely criticised, as someone in serious trouble

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in trouble and liable to be scolded, and literally describes something immersed in scalding liquid.

clue.text: Entertain no thoughts of taking just a pass degree!

definitions.text: no thoughts of taking just a pass degree!

explanation.surface: A student aims for a proper degree rather than a bare pass.
explanation.walkthrough: A British pass degree is a basic one; an honours degree is the higher course, so a student who rejects the pass will 'do the honours'.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as host, pouring drinks or carving, is to perform the hospitable duties; and literally to study for an honours degree.

clue.text: When life is difficult daily

explanation.surface: A tough period of life, day after day.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on The Times, a daily newspaper, and the Dickens novel title.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard times are a period of hardship; read as a newspaper name it suggests a daily paper.

clue.text: Fuel for an Air Force fellow in great distress

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed inside the word for great distress

parts.note: great distress is pain
RAF is the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: An airman badly in need of fuel for his aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is kerosene, burned in lamps, heaters and jet engines.

clue.text: An increase in alkalinity is sweet

explanation.surface: A chemistry result is described as pleasing.
explanation.walkthrough: Acidity falling means alkalinity rises; an acid drop is a sharp-tasting British boiled sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall in acidity raises alkalinity; and the name of a tangy boiled confection.

clue.text: Cereal production is indeed getting faster

indicators.note: with the next word split as in deed, the reworked cereal letters are said to be in it

parts.note: split as in deed; a deed is an action, and the in belongs with the container signal

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of the cereal, so its letters are reworked

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cereal maker reports that output is speeding up.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 'indeed' as 'in deed', so 'is in deed' places the reshuffled cereal inside the word for a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceleration is the process of gaining speed.

clue.text: Turn one's back on upsetting Common Market swindle

parts.note: to turn one's back on danger and run is to flee

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: EC, the European Community, was the old Common Market

explanation.surface: Walking away from a disruptive trading bloc's fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to cheat them out of money.

clue.text: Fish-hawk seen in very large quarry

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
a hunted animal is quarry or prey

explanation.surface: A bird of prey spotted in a big stone quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a large raptor that dives for fish.

clue.text: In Croatia I designated an assistant

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words Croatia I designated

explanation.surface: Someone in Croatia names a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant to someone senior.

clue.text: "-do not a prison make."

parts.note: the opening words of Lovelace's line from To Althea, from Prison are missing and must be supplied

explanation.walkthrough: Richard Lovelace's poem runs 'Stone walls do not a prison make, / Nor iron bars a cage.'
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation completes with the masonry barriers that open Lovelace's famous couplet.

clue.text: Less than 20cwt is unworthy of consideration

explanation.surface: A load under the weight limit is dismissed as negligible.
explanation.walkthrough: Twenty hundredweight (cwt) make an imperial ton; 'not on' is British for unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally short of the weight of twenty hundredweight; idiomatically, out of the question.

clue.text: At liberty to leave Rex in charge

indicators.note: the letter for the king is placed inside the word for charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A dog named Rex is released from custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone free is unrestrained and able to go.

clue.text: Anything but a long way off

explanation.surface: Someone denies being anywhere near the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: As an emphatic denial it means not at all; literally it means at a great distance from something.

clue.text: The one right belonging to others

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single entitlement owned by other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive form used for things owned by a group of people other than the speaker.

clue.text: Children's pliers

explanation.surface: Kids' gripping tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippers is British slang for small children, and also a pincer tool for gripping or cutting.

clue.text: North Surrey arranged child-care facility

indicators.note: the letters of the county name are put into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A creche is set up in the northern part of the county.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where young children are looked after during the day.
